data.title: UMG sues DistroKid for allegedly distributing AI 'slop' music
data.description:
Sept 15 (Reuters) - Universal Music Group sued DistroKid in Delaware federal court on Tuesday, accusing the online music distributor of infringing the label's copyrights and "flooding platforms with AI-generated 'slop' that siphons revenue and listeners from the legitimate artists."

The lawsuit accused DistroKid of bolstering its streaming numbers and revenue with mass-uploaded, bot-generated "spam" music as well as "thousands" of unlicensed versions of UMG recordings.

"At scale, DistroKid's conduct makes it more difficult for working and emerging artists to be discovered and compensated for their creative labor," the complaint said.

Spokespeople for DistroKid did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the lawsuit.

DistroKid is a distribution service that allows recording artists to upload music across online stores and streaming platforms. Spotify ( SPOT ), which is not named in the lawsuit, bought a minority stake in the company in 2018.

UMG's lawsuit said that a "massive portion" of DistroKid's music is either AI "slop" or copyright-infringing despite the distributor's assurances otherwise. In addition to alleged AI "slop," the label accused DistroKid of releasing thousands of tracks that are "remixed or speed-altered" UMG recordings, illegally sample UMG music, or otherwise violate its rights.

UMG said DistroKid violated its rights in at least 1,000 recordings by popular artists including, The Beatles, Drake, Lady Gaga and Rihanna. It asked the court for monetary damages and an order blocking DistroKid's alleged misconduct.

The complaint also said that DistroKid created many of its AI tracks using the AI music generator Suno. UMG has separately sued Suno for allegedly misusing its music for AI training.

The case is UMG Recordings Inc v. DistroKid LLC, U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware, No. 1:26-cv-01156.

For UMG: Glenn Pomerantz of Munger, Tolles & Olson

For DistroKid: attorney information not yet available

Read more:

Music labels sue AI companies Suno, Udio for US copyright infringement

(Reporting by Blake Brittain in Washington)

data.description:
Energy sector veteran brings regulatory and public utility expertise to help scale AI-powered energy market intelligence platform

SAN FRANCISCO--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Halcyon, the AI platform for energy, announced today that it has appointed Nick Chaset, CEO of Octopus Energy US and CEO of Uplight, to its Board of Directors as an Independent Director, effective September 1st, 2026.

“Adding Nick strengthens our board with a leader who knows what it takes to build and scale category-defining global businesses,” said Bruce Falck, CEO and Board Chair, Halcyon. “He brings a deep understanding of the regulatory processes supporting U.S. power markets and has well-established relationships with senior executives across the energy sector which we are excited to leverage to help us better serve our customers.”

Chaset is CEO of Octopus Energy US, where he runs both a retail electricity business and its flexibility services, and this month was also named CEO of Uplight, the demand-flexibility platform in which Octopus Energy Group recently took a majority stake. Prior to Octopus, he was the founding CEO of Ava Community Energy, growing the Bay Area community choice aggregator for over seven years to serve 1.7 million people. He also served as Chief of Staff to California Public Utilities Commission President Michael Picker and as a special advisor to Governor Jerry Brown on distributed energy resources.

"My work at Octopus and Uplight is about getting more out of the grid we have today. Delivering flexible solutions that are better, cheaper, and more reliable requires technology that transforms the high-volume high-velocity regulatory information firehose into a competitive advantage,” said Chaset. “That’s exactly what Halcyon does. Bruce has assembled an incredible team that is building technological infrastructure underpinning the rapidly growing energy market, and I'm grateful to be a part of it."

Chaset joins Falck and existing Halcyon board members Nat Bullard (Chief Strategy Officer & co-founder, Halcyon), Tyler Lancaster (Partner & Co-Head of Ventures, Energize Capital), and Tanuj Dutta (General Partner, Congruent Ventures).

Halcyon makes complex and fragmented energy information discoverable, actionable, and valuable. Unlike general-purpose AI tools, Halcyon is built on the most comprehensive catalog of energy regulatory data available — spanning all 50 U.S. state public utility commissions, every independent system operator (ISO) and regional transmission organization (RTO), the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), and state environmental agencies — and validated by energy domain experts to ensure its outputs are accurate enough to inform real business decisions.

Halcyon is the AI platform for energy. data.title: AutoZone Fourth-Quarter Comps May Miss Street Views Amid Soft Aftermarket Demand, UBS Says
data.description:
02:51 PM EDT, 09/15/2026 (MT Newswires) -- AutoZone's ( AZO ) fiscal fourth-quarter comparable sales are likely to miss Wall Street's projections amid soft aftermarket demand, though the print is expected to offer "line of sight" to earnings growth in 2027, UBS Securities said Tuesday.

The brokerage expects the auto parts retailer to post fourth-quarter domestic comparable sales growth of 2.5% when it reports results Sept. 22. The Street is looking for an increase of 3.6%, UBS said in a note to clients.

"At this point, we think it is well understood by the market that the aftermarket (industry) experienced softer demand during the period corresponding to (AutoZone's ( AZO ) fourth quarter)," UBS analysts Michael Lasser and Mark Carden wrote. "Most likely, the company's sales growth bottomed in June and experienced a modest acceleration in July and August."

AutoZone's ( AZO ) hub and megahub expansion are a key driver of market share gains, while store openings are set to provide a further boost to annual comp, according to the note. "Having 100 to 150 additional locations that are in the early stages of their life cycle could add 20 (basis points) or so to the company's annual comp," Lasser and Carden said.

The upcoming results are likely to mark a point at which the market will be able to have" line of sight" to bottom-line growth next year, according to UBS. "In fact, we think (AutoZone ( AZO )) can see mid-teens EPS growth in fiscal 2027 as the pieces of its model come together."

The company could present a case that it can generate "stable" comparable sales in the coming quarters, according to the analysts. "Together, these dynamics will help to calibrate models to expectations that are realistic."

Aftermarket industry conditions have remained generally durable, but trends decelerated across major peers over recent months due to factors such as pressure on core do-it-yourself, or DIY, consumers from higher gasoline prices, the brokerage said.

Last month, auto parts retailer Advance Auto Parts ( AAP ) lifted its full year-year earnings outlook even after its fiscal second-quarter comparable sales unexpectedly declined amid weakness in the DIY channel. data.title: US STOCKS-Wall Street dips as oil spikes and benchmark Treasury yields breach 5%
data.description:
(Updates to mid-afternoon trading)

* Indexes down: Dow 0.82%, S&P 0.47%, Nasdaq 0.78%

* Traders price in 92% chance of Fed rate hike on Wednesday

* Dave & Buster's slides after Q2 revenue miss

* Crypto firms sink on bitcoin weakness

By Stephen Culp and Tharuniyaa Lakshmi

NEW YORK, Sept 15 (Reuters) - Wall Street extended its slide on Tuesday, as rising U.S. Treasury yields, mounting debt concerns and soaring crude prices kept buyers on the sidelines.

All three major U.S. stock indexes were lower in a broad selloff that weighed on nearly every sector but energy. That sector benefited from expanding hostilities in the Middle East, which included new attacks on Saudi Arabia's energy infrastructure.

"It is kind of a quiet market, but then you look at the advance/decline line, at the number of stocks that are moving in one direction, it is demonstratively to the downside over the last probably two weeks," said Paul Nolte, senior wealth adviser and market strategist at Murphy & Sylvest in Elmhurst, Illinois.

The Federal Reserve has convened for its two-day monetary policy meeting, which is due to culminate on Wednesday with the central bank's rate decision. With recent economic data showing the labor market on solid footing, while war-related energy price pressures are morphing into broader, systemic inflation, the central bank is expected to implement a 25-basis-point increase to its Fed funds target rate - its first interest rate hike in over three years.

In the wake of last week's hot inflation data and the near 25% jump in U.S. crude prices over the last two weeks, financial markets have priced in a near-certain 92.3% likelihood of a rate hike on Wednesday, up from 33.1% one month ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

"This will probably be not a one-and-done, but a series of rate increases," Nolte said. "It will be dependent on oil; that is really the source of inflation and it's starting to seep into other parts of the market."

As rate-hike bets increase, global bond yields resumed their upward climb, with benchmark U.S. Treasury yields breaching the 5% mark for the first time since 2007.

Rising interest rates are increasing the pressure on heavily indebted borrowers, including companies that have placed big bets on AI.

Those worries exacerbated mounting fears over AI's destructive potential and growing opposition to the construction of data centers, which came to a head on Monday and dragged the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index 5.9% lower.

The semiconductor index, which has helped drive broader stock market gains this year, failed to meaningfully recover from Monday's rout, eking out a 0.3% gain.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 429.96 points, or 0.82%, to 51,991.24, the S&P 500 lost 36.03 points, or 0.47%, to 7,583.95 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 204.17 points, or 0.78%, to 25,982.25.

Among the 11 major sectors of the S&P 500, consumer discretionary stocks were the biggest percentage losers, while energy, buoyed by rising crude, advanced 2.3%.

Dave & Buster's tumbled 19.6% following the company's second-quarter revenue miss.

Waystar ( WAY ) rose 7.3% after Reuters reported the healthcare software firm is exploring options, including a potential sale.

Weakness in bitcoin weighed down crypto firms Coinbase and Strategy 6.9% and 3.5%, respectively.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 2.47-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. There were 97 new highs and 539 new lows on the NYSE.

On the Nasdaq, 1,413 stocks rose and 3,281 fell as declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 2.32-to-1 ratio.

The S&P 500 posted 12 new 52-week highs and 15 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 40 new highs and 239 new lows.

data.title: Olympics-LA28 could generate up to $40.6 billion for region, study says
data.description:
LOS ANGELES, Sept 15 (Reuters) - The 2028 Los Angeles Olympic and Paralympic Games could generate as much as $40.6 billion in economic output and support up to 224,000 jobs across the Greater Los Angeles region, according to a study released on Tuesday.

The analysis by the Los Angeles County Economic Development Corporation, commissioned by LA28, estimated a range of $20.5 billion to $40.6 billion in economic activity during the years of preparation for the Games and through their conclusion in 2028.

"The scale and breadth of the economic activity associated with the 2028 Games is significant, even when viewed through a conservative lens," said Stephen Cheung, President & CEO of LAEDC.

"Our analysis shows the impact reaching across the regional economy, from jobs and labor income to local businesses, visitor spending, and long-term investment. Importantly, these findings reflect a range of potential outcomes, providing a transparent picture of the economic benefits the Games could generate for Greater Los Angeles."

The estimates cover Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside, San Bernardino and Ventura counties, and include spending on Games operations, transportation and security, capital projects, visitor activity and expenditures by independently funded organizations involved in staging the event.

Games-related infrastructure investment, including transportation, airport, mobility, accessibility and venue upgrades, would be the largest source of economic impact, the report said.

It estimated that about $8.35 billion in such investment has been accelerated or undertaken in connection with the event.

NO-BUILD GAMES

LA28 has promoted a "no-build" strategy that relies largely on existing venues and temporary facilities, rather than construction of new permanent Olympic sites.

The study projected that the Games could bring about 2 million visitors to the region. Direct spending by non-resident visitors in Los Angeles County was estimated at between $1.6 billion and $4.3 billion, potentially benefiting hotels, restaurants, retailers and entertainment businesses.

The report also forecast $5.1 billion to $5.9 billion in combined federal, state and local tax revenue associated with Games-related economic activity.

The job estimates include positions in construction, transportation, hospitality, accommodation, security and administrative services, among other industries.

LA28 said it aims to direct 75% of its addressable procurement spending to Greater Los Angeles businesses, with 25% targeted toward local and small businesses.

The LAEDC said it used two methodologies to develop the estimates: a more conservative framework focused on new outside spending entering the region, and an IMPLAN input-output model that measures broader gross economic activity.

Los Angeles will host the Summer Olympics for the third time, after 1932 and 1984, and the Paralympic Games for the first time.

(Reporting by Rory Carroll in Los Angeles, editing by Pritha Sarkar)

data.title: Sanders and Bannon call for AI limits as public unease grows
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Sept 15 (Reuters) - Progressive U.S. Senator Bernie Sanders and Steve Bannon, a close ally of President Donald Trump, called on Tuesday for restrictions on AI systems, uniting two political adversaries around concerns that the technology will harm humans.

The two appeared at the same Washington gathering and warned of the potentially catastrophic consequences AI poses to humanity, as concern about its risks spreads beyond Washington and Silicon Valley.

Speaking first, Sanders, a self-described democratic socialist, warned about the "growing threat" of AI and said the industry needed to be regulated with binding safety rules.

"AI has the potential to eliminate tens of millions of jobs, wiping out entire professions and making it harder for our young people to enter the workforce."

He added, "As many scientists believe could happen, this technology will escape human control with potentially catastrophic consequences."

Sanders drew applause from the room when he criticized tech executives for centralizing control over AI technology, including SpaceX CEO and former Trump adviser Elon Musk.

"Last month, we learned that AI has been used for the first time ever to create new viruses. In the wrong hands, this could lead to new bioweapons and a potential global pandemic that could lead to the deaths of tens of millions of people," Sanders said.

Sanders called on Trump to negotiate a treaty with Chinese President Xi Jinping at their summit next week to pause AI development.

Bannon, a former White House strategist during Trump's first presidential term, has criticized Trump's approach to overseeing AI, placing the blame for the president's unwillingness to regulate the technology squarely on tech companies. On his Monday podcast, Bannon said Congress should not pass laws that prohibit states from enforcing their own rules for the technology.

On Tuesday, Bannon called AI the defining issue of our time.

"Here's what we have to do first: to slow down the pace so that we can understand exactly what's going on," Bannon said. He praised Sanders for the way he summarized the risks of AI and said the country has to rise above partisanship on the issue.

"I don't think you could find any too harder partisans than Bernie Sanders on the left and Steve Bannon on the right," he said.

Bannon said Congress will take too long to pass legislation slowing the development of AI. "This is going to have to be executive action," Bannon said.

He said the U.S. must cut off China from American-made computer chips.

UNLIKELY BEDFELLOWS

The decision of Sanders and Bannon, who are on opposite ends of America's ideological divide, to speak at the same gathering on Tuesday underscores how concerns over AI and data centers are cutting across party lines and producing unlikely political bedfellows.

Trump on Monday downplayed concerns expressed by industry leaders over the weekend about the misuse of artificial intelligence harming people, saying the U.S. already has guardrails in place for the powerful technology.

Backing Trump's position on Tuesday, Republican U.S. House Speaker Mike Johnson said there cannot be a moratorium on artificial ‌intelligence development without losing the competitive edge to China and that AI companies can regulate themselves.

"They can self-regulate. They don't need the government to ​tell them to slow it down. If they want ​to slow it down, they should," Johnson told reporters.

The view that regulations will harm U.S. companies' ability to compete with their Chinese counterparts is shared by tech executives, including Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang.

Recent surveys have found majorities of Americans worry the technology could be used to eliminate jobs, raise costs for families or otherwise cause social harm.

BACK FROM RECESS

The U.S. House of Representatives ended its long summer break on Monday, with members in the House and Senate holding private conversations about whether or not to legislate on AI, especially after Trump said there was no need for legislative action.

Congress has been criticized in the past for lacking the collective expertise to rein in or regulate technology companies.

Speaking to Reuters, Republican Senator Bernie Moreno of Ohio said, "This process of legislating takes so long. Imagine AI four years in. We're dealing with stuff that isn't even relevant in four years."

Residents in several states have also challenged proposals for new data centers, a critical component of the AI boom. According to a Reuters/Ipsos poll published in June, 77% of Americans worry AI-driven data centers will raise electricity costs. 

Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon captured public attention last week when he said he resigned from the company, in part because the "people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade."

Also on Tuesday, Andrew Ferguson, the chairman of the U.S. Federal Trade Commission, expressed suspicions over AI companies seeking antitrust exemptions while they also lobby for new regulations.

Reuters previously reported that U.S. senators are debating a bill that would block states from enforcing their own laws governing certain risks posed by AI models. Previously, efforts to restrict state AI laws failed in the U.S. Senate.

Sanders and Bannon addressed the same event as AFL-CIO President Liz Shuler, who leads the largest federation of labor unions in the U.S.  

Sanders, along with House progressive Rep. Greg Casar, has called for the U.S. to pass legislation halting development of AI tools that are capable of "overthrowing or undermining the U.S. government," until the government creates a new agency to police the technology. Casar and Sanders have not released specifics.  

(Reporting by Courtney Rozen. Additional reporting by Tim Reid, Alexandra Alper and Richard Cowan. Editing by David Gregorio and Nick Zieminski)

data.title: Wall St wobbles as rising oil and Treasury yields stoke investor unease
data.description:
NEW YORK, Sept 15 (Reuters) - Wall Street extended its slide on Tuesday, as rising U.S. Treasury yields, mounting debt concerns and soaring crude prices kept buyers on the sidelines.

All three major U.S. stock indexes were lower in a broad selloff that weighed on nearly every sector but energy. That sector benefited from expanding hostilities in the Middle East, which included new attacks on Saudi Arabia's energy infrastructure.

"It is kind of a quiet market, but then you look at the advance/decline line, at the number of stocks that are moving in one direction, it is demonstratively to the downside over the last probably two weeks," said Paul Nolte, senior wealth adviser and market strategist at Murphy & Sylvest in Elmhurst, Illinois.

The Federal Reserve has convened for its two-day monetary policy meeting, which is due to culminate on Wednesday with the central bank's rate decision. With recent economic data showing the labor market on solid footing, while war-related energy price pressures are morphing into broader, systemic inflation, the central bank is expected to implement a 25-basis-point increase to its Fed funds target rate - its first interest rate hike in over three years.

In the wake of last week's hot inflation data and the near 25% jump in U.S. crude prices over the last two weeks, financial markets have priced in a near-certain 92.3% likelihood of a rate hike on Wednesday, up from 33.1% one month ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

"This will probably be not a one-and-done, but a series of rate increases," Nolte said. "It will be dependent on oil; that is really the source of inflation and it's starting to seep into other parts of the market."

As rate-hike bets increase, global bond yields resumed their upward climb, with benchmark U.S. Treasury yields breaching the 5% mark for the first time since 2007.

Rising interest rates are increasing the pressure on heavily indebted borrowers, including companies that have placed big bets on AI.

Those worries exacerbated mounting fears over AI's destructive potential and growing opposition to the construction of data centers, which came to a head on Monday and dragged the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index 5.9% lower.

The semiconductor index, which has helped drive broader stock market gains this year, failed to meaningfully recover from Monday's rout, eking out a 0.3% gain.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 429.96 points, or 0.82%, to 51,991.24, the S&P 500 lost 36.03 points, or 0.47%, to 7,583.95 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 204.17 points, or 0.78%, to 25,982.25.

Among the 11 major sectors of the S&P 500, consumer discretionary stocks were the biggest percentage losers, while energy, buoyed by rising crude, advanced 2.3%.

Dave & Buster's tumbled 19.6% following the company's second-quarter revenue miss.

Waystar rose 7.3% after Reuters reported the healthcare software firm is exploring options, including a potential sale.

Weakness in bitcoin weighed down crypto firms Coinbase and Strategy 6.9% and 3.5%, respectively.

The S&P 500 posted 12 new 52-week highs and 15 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 40 new highs and 239 new lows.

data.title: Ferrovalle and INFORM Partner to Advance AI-Powered Intermodal Operations in Mexico City
data.description:
INFORM's Syncrotess Optimization Plus platform to power major Smart Yard automation initiative at Latin America's flagship inland rail freight hub at Ferrovalle Intermodal in Mexico City. The optimization software will support yard, equipment, and train operations across two operational areas while working alongside Ferrovalle's existing in-house Terminal Operating System (TOS). Go-live is targeted for June 2027.

ATLANTA and CHICAGO, Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- INFORM, a global leader in AI-driven logistics and operational optimization, today announced Ferrovalle has selected its Syncrotess Optimization Plus software to power a major Smart Yard initiative in Mexico City. Ferrovalle operates one of Mexico's most important rail freight hubs and serves as a key last-mile connection for rail traffic moving through the Valley of Mexico. Its intermodal division handled around 550,000 TEUs in 2025, making it one of Latin America's largest inland intermodal operations.

Taking automation beyond the gate
With its Smart Yard project, Ferrovalle is extending its automation further into terminal operations. Planning container storage, equipment deployment, and train loading and discharge currently still relies to a significant degree on manual criteria and dispatcher experience. Syncrotess Optimization Plus will use operational data from Ferrovalle's existing systems to provide greater operational transparency and generate coordinated, continuously updated recommendations.

"Smart Yard represents an important next step in Ferrovalle's digital transformation and in our vision for the future of intermodal operations," said Francisco Fabila, Managing Director of Ferrovalle. "Our objective is clear: every train, every railcar, every container and every truck moving through our operation should have real-time digital visibility, supported with automated data capture, advanced analytics and AI-driven decision support by INFORM. By integrating these capabilities into our existing digital ecosystem, we are giving our teams better tools to operate more efficiently, consistently, and safely. Ultimately, technology is not the objective in itself; it is an enabler to deliver a more predictable, reliable and customer-focused service."

The solution combines INFORM's Yard Optimizer, Crane Optimizer, Vehicle Optimizer, and Train Load Optimizer. The initial optimized fleet includes eight RTG cranes, four reach stackers, and 14 terminal tractors. Ferrovalle aims to increase equipment throughput, improve the ratio of billable moves to total handling volume, and meet defined service-level targets for truck handling, train loading, and train discharging.

A key feature of the project is its hybrid architecture. Rather than replacing Ferrovalle's internally developed TOS, Syncrotess Optimization Plus will operate as an additional optimization layer, exchanging train consist data, load plans, container status, clearance information, and operational updates.

Optimization within a complex customs environment
The project covers two specific yards: customs-cleared and customs-controlled yards. The optimization must maintain this separation while also accounting for different processes for maritime and cross-border containers.

Dedicated inspection and loading areas will be integrated into the workflow through automated tractor assignments and status exchanges with Ferrovalle's TOS. Additionally, integration with the terminal's Equipment Control System (ECS) enables automatic weight verification during routine crane lifts, eliminating separate weighing stops and keeping cargo moving.

Customs clearance will be incorporated directly into operational decision-making. Before Syncrotess Optimization Plus assigns a container for train loading, Ferrovalle's TOS confirms that the necessary customs and documentation clearance has been granted. Only cleared containers can be released for loading.

"Ferrovalle already has a sophisticated digital infrastructure, so this project is not about replacing existing systems," said Dr. Eva Savelsberg, Senior Vice President Terminal & Distribution Center Logistics at INFORM. "The task is to connect the available data with intelligent optimization and coordinate decisions across yard, equipment, and train operations."

To further streamline intermodal rail transfers, the Train Load Optimizer will additionally automate a planning process that is currently largely manual. It generates optimized train load plans based on available containers, train configurations, operational restrictions, and clearance status. Planners remain able to review and adjust the proposed plans when required.

The contract was signed in early September 2026, with go-live planned approximately nine months later in June 2027.

About INFORM
INFORM develops software solutions that enable better decision-making in industrial and logistics processes as well as in the financial sector, from risk management and fraud prevention to compliance. Founded in 1969, the company is a trusted partner to more than 2,000 active customers worldwide. Built on AI and operations research, INFORM combines rigorous scientific methods with deep industry expertise. Its approach brings together human knowledge and machine intelligence to turn data into informed, actionable decisions. INFORM's solutions integrate into existing processes and help organizations reduce risk, improve efficiency, and plan with greater confidence, while upholding data privacy and ethical standards. data.title: Ramsey Theory Group Commits $600,000 Annually to Back Exceptional Students on Nontraditional Paths
data.description:
NEW YORK, Sept. 15, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Ramsey Theory Group today announced a $600,000 annual commitment to identify and support exceptional people whose abilities may not be fully reflected by conventional academic or career trajectories, launching the Dan Herbatschek Fellowship for its inaugural 2027 cohort.

Image: DAN HERBATSCHEK HEAD SHOT

The new fellowship will select just 10 fellows each year, providing each with a $60,000 allocation and a highly structured 12-month program combining rigorous study, individualized mentorship and practical work across mathematics, technology and business.

Applications are now open through January 15, 2027 at https://www.herbatschekfellowship.org/

The fellowship grew in part from founder Dan Herbatschek's own unconventional educational path. After some time away from formal study, Herbatschek returned to college at Columbia University, where he studied intellectual history, philosophy, and mathematics.

That experience shaped a central idea behind the program: an interrupted path can obscure ability without defining it.

“We are too quick to mistake continuity for merit and interruption for a lack of seriousness,” said Dan Herbatschek, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Ramsey Theory Group. “A conventional résumé can reveal accomplishment, but it cannot measure every form of intelligence, discipline, courage, or promise. … There are extraordinarily capable people whose potential is hidden behind gaps, detours or circumstances that have little to do with their ability. This fellowship is designed to find them—and give them the time, resources, mentorship and intellectual challenge to show what they can actually do.”

Beyond a Scholarship: $60,000 Plus a Year of Rigorous Development

The Dan Herbatschek Fellowship is deliberately structured as more than a traditional financial award.

Each fellow will receive a $60,000 individual allocation while completing a 12-month intellectual and professional circuit that moves from foundational study in logic, probability, linear algebra, algorithms, writing and argument through models and code, applied practice in a business setting and an independent final contribution.

Fellows will also receive individualized plans, sustained mentorship, recurring progress reviews and exposure to practical problems. Each participant will be expected to complete substantial final work, including a capstone and presentation or defense, as well as a defined plan for the next stage of their academic or professional development.

“The distance between talent and opportunity is not theoretical. It is made of concrete things: tuition, time, housing, guidance, professional networks, practical experience, and the freedom to take an intellectual risk without placing the rest of one's life at risk,” Herbatschek said. “Financial support is therefore essential. It buys time, stability, and the right to concentrate. But money alone cannot create direction, intellectual community, practical judgment, or the confidence that grows when serious people take your ideas seriously.”

Looking Beyond the Conventional Résumé

The fellowship is intended for candidates whose traditional academic or professional records may not fully capture their potential.

That may include students returning after an interruption; community-college and transfer students; immigrants and first-generation students; people balancing education with work or family responsibilities; self-taught programmers; and candidates moving between the humanities and computation.

But an unconventional path or personal difficulty alone will not qualify an applicant.

Candidates will be evaluated on intellectual ability, seriousness, initiative, fit with the program and the likely impact of substantial support. Fellows will be held to demanding standards of participation, intellectual honesty, professional integrity and completed work.

“We will not lower our expectations of fellows because their paths have been difficult,” Herbatschek said. “We will see their talent more accurately and give it the demanding support it deserves. Care and rigor are not opposites.”

The Idea Behind the Fellowship

Herbatschek's own experience informs that approach.

Life circumstances did not enable Herbatschek to go straight to college. After taking a break for a few years, he attended Columbia University and pursued work spanning intellectual history, philosophy, logic and mathematics. His research examined mathematics, artificial languages and changing conceptions of time during the Scientific Revolution.

Herbatschek has said that people who believed in him before his record told the full story helped change the trajectory of his own life. “They did more than encourage me. They gave me time, guidance, opportunity, trust, and entry into intellectual worlds I could not have reached alone. They saw me and helped convert possibility into a path.”

“The Dan Herbatschek Fellowship at Ramsey Theory Group is an expression of my gratitude to them,” Herbatschek said.

He later founded Ramsey Theory Group, a technology holding company with an integrated operating platform that builds, owns, incubates, and scales businesses and intellectual property across the digital economy. The group’s portfolio spans technology services, enterprise AI, cybersecurity, quantitative analysis, entertainment marketing, proprietary software, and vertical SaaS. Ramsey Theory Group combines capital allocation, infrastructure, R&D, and strategic capabilities to create and compound long-term value.

The fellowship extends a similar philosophy to talent development: combining foundational knowledge and rigorous thinking with practical work.

“A résumé tells you where someone has been; it doesn't necessarily tell you how far they can go,” Herbatschek said. “Some exceptional people simply need someone willing to look past the route they took and examine the quality of their thinking, the seriousness of their work and what they might accomplish if given a real opportunity.”

Herbatschek said he ultimately sees the fellowship not as a recognition of his own accomplishments, but as a vehicle for creating opportunities for others. “Although this fellowship bears my name, I do not want it to be a monument. I want it to be an instrument: a structure through which gratitude becomes opportunity and opportunity becomes work of lasting value. … I cannot give another person a linear past. But through this fellowship, we can help make possible a less constrained future.”

Applications Open for the 2027 Dan Herbatschek Fellowship

Applications for the inaugural 2027 Dan Herbatschek Fellowship are open now and close January 15, 2027.

At a glance:

  • Annual commitment: $600,000
  • Fellows selected: 10 per year

* Treasury yields at highest since 2007, Bunds since 2009

* Stocks slip as Middle East tensions weigh

By Chibuike Oguh

NEW YORK, Sept 15 (Reuters) - Global stocks were lower on Tuesday, continuing a selloff from the previous session, after U.S. Treasury yields hit their highest level since 2007 and with oil prices firmly above $100 per barrel.

U.S. Treasury yields have risen over the past month as investors weigh expectations for higher interest rates, resilient economic growth and concerns about the country's long-term fiscal outlook given rising inflation.

Investors' attention was turning to the Federal Reserve, with traders anticipating at least a quarter-point hike. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has been reluctant to provide guidance on the future path of rates.

On Wall Street, all three main indexes were trading lower, with consumer discretionary, communication services and financial stocks driving losses. Energy shares were the biggest gainers.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.89%, the S&P 500 lost 0.46%, and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 0.69%.

Europe's STOXX 600 fell 0.29% after hitting its lowest level since June 12. The European tech stock index rose 0.10%, after shedding more than 2% on Monday.

"We have to recognize that this is a very appropriate move in the Treasury market and there should be zero shock factor in the fact that we've had an exuberant economic backdrop, we had earnings growth that just hit 30% last quarter and we have a geopolitical conflict that's driving up commodity prices," said Edison Byzyka, chief investment officer at Credent Wealth Management.

"I think the Fed needs to absolutely raise rates tomorrow. If the Fed does not raise rates by at least a quarter of a (percentage) point, we're going to see the bond market just punish the Treasury market."

U.S. 10-year Treasury yields hit peaks not seen since 2007 ahead of the Fed's rate decision on Wednesday. The yield on benchmark U.S. 10-year notes rose 3.47 basis points to 4.996%.

German Bund yields, the euro area's benchmark, rose to their highest level in over 17 years at 3.56%.

The Bank of Japan is widely expected to raise its interest rate by 25 bps to 1.25% at the end of its two-day meeting on Friday and signal more tightening ahead. Policymakers are seeking to shore up the yen after intervention helped steer the currency away from a 40-year low.

As AI models scale beyond two trillion parameters, new memory technology is needed to increase capacity and throughput while reducing power consumption. TeRAM is validating its technology and targeting initial customer production in 2029.

“Memory is the constraint on AI progress, and incremental improvements will not be enough. Charlie saw this early. He is a rare founder who connects AI architecture, memory physics, and semiconductor manufacturing, and has assembled an extraordinary team to realize his vision. TeRAM is building the memory platform the next generation of AI requires,” said Brian Schechter, a partner at Primary Venture Partners and the lead investor in the seed round.

Under the AI scaling law, frontier models become more capable as parameter counts and context windows grow. Together with agentic workflows, these advances have accelerated AI adoption. Since mid-2025, agentic inference has overtaken model training as the main driver of AI compute and token generation. This has shifted the memory wall from HBM capacity during training to memory bandwidth during inference. Generating each output token requires a pass through the entire model and its trillions of parameters, making memory bandwidth a bottleneck for AI compute, whether the model resides in on-chip SRAM or off-chip HBM modules.

TeRAM is developing memory and packaging technologies to integrate 3D SRAM directly onto AI compute chips. Designed for demanding thermal conditions, these technologies aim to deliver unprecedented memory bandwidth at the lowest possible power consumption.

“I am grateful for Brian’s conviction in our mission and for all the investors supporting this groundbreaking roadmap,” said Charlie Cheng, CEO of TeRAM. “Developing a new memory technology is an ambitious undertaking. We are fortunate to have investors who back our vision with both capital and hands-on support.”

Primary, B Capital, Hyperion, and SemiAnalysis Capital co-led the round, joined by Alumni Ventures and Lightscape Partners, which closed on September 10, 2026. The consortium brings together deep insights and go-to-market reach in the AI ecosystem, as well as broad reaches into all corners of the capital market. The funding will enable TeRAM to validate its technology and scale the team to build the customized 3D SRAM memory chips for the initial datacenter customers.

TeRAM’s founders bring more than 80 years of combined experience developing semiconductor memory technology. The team has also collaborated closely on AI compute system-on-chip (SoC) projects with several leading hyperscalers and AI infrastructure companies. This combination of memory and compute expertise helps TeRAM understand the challenges facing future AI platforms and develop custom 3D SRAM to address each customer’s capacity, bandwidth, and power needs.

data.title: Fed Seen Delivering Rate Hike to Avoid Disappointing Markets, Goldman Says
data.description:
01:22 PM EDT, 09/15/2026 (MT Newswires) -- The Federal Reserve will likely raise its policy rate on Wednesday to avoid disappointing markets that almost fully price in a hike, Goldman Sachs said.

As the Federal Open Market Committee kicked off its two-day policy meeting on Tuesday, Goldman insisted that it doesn't see a strong economic case for a tighter policy at this point.

Official data released last week showed consumer inflation and producer prices hit three-month highs in August as energy costs rose.

"We added a 25 (basis-point) rate hike to our forecast after the August CPI, which had little impact on our inflation view but pushed market pricing of a hike to 90%, high enough that the FOMC will likely want to avoid the market reaction from staying on hold," Goldman said in a note sent Monday night.

Markets are currently pricing in a 93% probability that the FOMC will lift its benchmark lending rate by 25 basis points on Wednesday, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

In a note e-mailed Monday, UBS Securities projected a quarter-percentage-point rate increase this week, while predicting the Fed's latest "dot plot" to signal another hike later in 2026.

Goldman, however, said that the FOMC may avoid signaling further hikes in both the policy statement and the Summary of Economic Projections document that includes anonymous expectations on interest rates, dubbed the dot plot.

Goldman expects the dot plot to show a slim FOMC majority of 10 members leaning toward a single hike this year. However, there's a risk that a majority could back two increases "if more participants than we expect see a hike this week as a normal response to higher oil prices," according to the Wall Street giant.

Brent crude prices have jumped 19% so far this month after notching gains in both August and July, amid an intensifying conflict in the Middle East that have fueled fears of prolonged supply disruptions.

Goldman said the impact of one-time factors that keep inflation well above the 2% target is fading, citing an improvement in core personal consumption expenditure inflation to a 2.5% pace over the last three months.

"Inflation expectations are not at immediate risk of unanchoring (and) ... the economy is not overheated," the brokerage said.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh is unlikely to provide a clear path forward for policy when he speaks at the post-meeting press conference, according to Goldman.

"Warsh could say that before deciding on further steps, the FOMC will 'carefully assess' incoming data or will want to see upcoming inflation reports or how the underlying inflation trend evolves, which all hint at waiting a bit longer to collect more information," the brokerage said.

data.title: Bristol Myers sues Amgen over proposed Opdivo biosimilar
data.description:
Sept 15 (Reuters) - Bristol Myers Squibb ( BMY ) and Ono Pharmaceutical ( OPHLF ) have sued Amgen ( AMGN ) in Delaware federal court, seeking to block Amgen's ( AMGN ) proposed U.S. biosimilar of their blockbuster cancer immunotherapy drug Opdivo.

* The lawsuit, filed last week and made public on Monday, alleges that Amgen's ( AMGN ) biosimilar would infringe several patents.

* Opdivo earned Bristol Myers more than $5.9 billion in revenue in the United States last year, according to a company report.

* An Amgen spokesperson on Tuesday declined to comment on the complaint, citing pending litigation.

* Spokespeople for Bristol Myers and Ono did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

* Biosimilars are based on existing versions of biologic drugs and are comparable to generic versions of traditional pharmaceuticals. Unlike traditional drugs, complex biologics are made from living cells and cannot be copied exactly.

* Bristol Myers and Ono, which co-developed Opdivo, allege that Amgen's ( AMGN ) biosimilar would infringe seven U.S. patents covering the drug, and asked the court to block sales of the biosimilar while their patents remain in force.

* Opdivo has been approved in the U.S. to treat advanced or metastatic cancers, including ​melanoma, non-small cell lung cancer and kidney cancer.

* Bristol Myers and Ono settled a patent dispute with Merck ( MRK ) in 2017 over its rival blockbuster cancer drug Keytruda. Under the settlement, Merck ( MRK ) agreed to pay $625 million and a share of Keytruda royalties through 2023.

* Bristol Myers said in a report filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission in February that it expects to maintain patent exclusivity over Opdivo until 2028.

The case is Bristol-Myers Squibb Co. ( BMY ) v. Amgen Inc. ( AMGN ), U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware, No. 1:26-cv-01134.
